findings.title: `organization_context.member` can be `None`, raising `AttributeError`
findings.body: In `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get`, `enable_advanced` accesses `organization_context.member.has_global_access` whenever `request.user.is_superuser` is false. On `RpcUserOrganizationContext`, `member` is optional (`RpcOrganizationMember | None`) and can be `None` (for example, for system/API token requests or non-member contexts). When a non-superuser calls this endpoint in such a context, evaluating `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'`, breaking all GET requests to the audit logs endpoint even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested.

findings.title: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` crashes on `datetime` ordering and `enable_advanced_features` is rejected by `self.paginate`
findings.body:
When `optimized_pagination=true` is used, `self.paginate` is called with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator`, `order_by="-datetime"`, and `enable_advanced_features=True`. This fails in two ways:
1. `Endpoint.paginate` only forwards `paginator_kwargs` (not arbitrary `**kwargs` like `enable_advanced_features`) to the paginator constructor, so passing `enable_advanced_features=True` directly to `self.paginate()` raises `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'`.
2. `OptimizedCursorPaginator` subclasses `BasePaginator` rather than `DateTimePaginator`: its `get_item_key` calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` directly on `item.datetime` (a `datetime.datetime` instance), raising `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`, and its `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting it back to a `datetime` for comparing against a `DateTimeField`.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets cause `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported` on Django `QuerySet` slicing
findings.body: Both `BasePaginator.get_result` (lines 182-184, when `cursor.is_prev` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 880-886, when `cursor.offset < 0` with `enable_advanced_features=True` or `cursor.is_prev=True`) pass a negative `start_offset` (and potentially negative `stop`) into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Contrary to the comments claiming Django ORM handles negative slicing, Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly forbids negative slice bounds (`if (k.start is not None and k.start < 0) or (k.stop is not None and k.stop < 0): raise ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.')`). Any request supplying a cursor with a negative offset (e.g. `?cursor=0:-10:1` on any endpoint using `BasePaginator`/`Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator`) will raise an unhandled `ValueError` (HTTP 500).
